gaussian16._irc_recorrect_default_note: 🟢 [§39.136(2), 02_METHOD_SPEC.md, proposer13 ruled/engineer14 concurred, S3 wave-1] `recorrect=never` added to `irc_forward`/`irc_reverse` as the PRODUCTION DEFAULT for every future fresh (non-restart) IRC job, project-wide -- NOT scoped to any single reaction. Basis: `recorrect=never` is the proven fix for the corrector-oscillation crash that killed both R-A arms under the original (default-recorrection) setting, confirmed at DEFAULT step size by stage4 (§39.125) -- cheap, no point-count multiplier, unlike `StepSize=2`/`f=0.20` (adopted ONLY as a per-direction escalation if that direction's own IRC shows a `Bulirsch-Stoer... not Converging` warning, never as a blanket default: ~5x the points/core-h for the same arc). `maxpoints=30` stays explicit and unchanged -- already satisfies §39.136(2)'s "EXPLICIT maxpoints" requirement, this route is built via `qc_adapter.sh`'s `sei_qc_input` reading straight from this fixed template, not any per-tool builder default that could silently omit it. 🔴 [critic17, wave-1 review #2 -- corrects this note's own earlier scoping] Also applied to `irc_forward_rcfc`/`irc_reverse_rcfc`: the corrector-oscillation failure mode is a property of the CORRECTOR, not of where the Hessian came from (fresh CalcFC vs. read-from-.chk/rcfc) -- an initial 'restart jobs are structurally different, leave them out' scoping was wrong and has been reverted. See `_irc_rcfc_note` below: the rcfc switch is OFF today (`irc_hessian_source=calcfc`, confirmed in `config/b0_reactions.json`), so wave-1 was never exposed to this gap, but leaving it unfixed would have handed whoever flips that switch the exact default corrector that killed both R-A arms, with nothing to flag it.
gaussian16._stability_test_note: 🔴 [linear-hopping-frog plan, Track A item 2, coder] Diagnostic ONLY -- single-point wavefunction stability test (Gaussian's `stable=opt`), NOT a production job_type wired into any plan Item. Built to tell apart a genuine SCF/orbital instability from a basis-linear-dependency artifact along `U56_RA_scan`'s IRC (recurring `largest beta MO coefficient` warning, 32-39, worsening along the path). No opt/freq: cheap by design. See tools/build_u56_ra_stability_probe.py. 🔴 [critic14] `nosymm` here is NOT the geometry-drift reason `_nosymm_requirement` documents for the opt family (this route never moves the nuclei) -- it is a DIFFERENT, stability-specific reason: if G16 detects point-group symmetry in the input orientation, it can restrict the stability search to symmetry-adapted rotations of the wavefunction, missing a symmetry-LOWERING instability -- exactly the false-negative direction proposer10's falsifiability statement (39.113(e)) depends on being absent. The source IRC geometry was itself computed under `nosymm` (relaxed_scan/irc_forward are both in `_nosymm_required_job_types`); the probe must not silently reintroduce symmetry the geometry's own generation excluded.

gaussian16._ts_method: 🔴 [내 결정 — proposer 확인 요망] ORCA 판 P1 은 NEB-TS(반응물↔생성물 양끝단)를 썼다. G16 에는 NEB 가 없다. 가장 가까운 양끝단 대응이 QST2 이므로 그것으로 포팅했고, 실패하면 반응물 기하에서 opt=(ts,calcfc) 단끝단으로 폴백한다. 어느 경로를 탔는지는 ts_method.json 에 기록된다. P1 의 목적은 'TS 1건 완주 단가' 측정이므로 두 경로 모두 그 목적을 만족하지만, 단가는 경로에 따라 달라진다 — 회신 해석 시 반드시 함께 읽어라.
gaussian16._relaxed_scan_note: 🔴 [U56-2, §39.39(d)/(h)] relaxed scan = scan → opt=ts → freq → IRC 체인의 scan 단계. G16 은 opt=modredundant + 추가 입력 섹션의 `B i j S N step` 줄로 relaxed surface scan 을 돈다. 좌표(어느 결합을 얼마나)는 이 route 가 아니라 **deck builder(sei_pilot/b0f_deck.py)가 role→index mapping(§39.26(d))에서 만든 ModRedundant 섹션**으로 온다 — 원자 index 를 config/route 에 박는 것이 금지이기 때문이다('BY CHEMICAL ROLE, NEVER BY ATOM INDEX', b0_reactions.json). nosymm 은 §39.39(b) 조건 2(인증된 끝단에서 출발하는 모든 route).
gaussian16._grid_parity_note: 🔴 [§39.41(b), proposer7/lead 2026-08-20] Int(Grid=UltraFine) 는 TS/IRC family 전체(ts_opt, ts_opt_from_guess, ts_qst2, irc_forward/reverse(+_rcfc), relaxed_scan)에 endpoint_* route 와 동일하게 들어간다 — C-8.1: grid 가 다르면 다른 표면이고, 다른 표면의 n_imag==0 은 우리가 인증한 그 표면의 사실이 아니다. nosymm 누락과 같은 결함 부류, 같은 발견 방법(아티팩트 직접 읽기). tests/test_endpoint_route_parity.py 가 TS/IRC route 까지 surface token 동일성을 고정한다.
gaussian16._irc_rcfc_note: 🔴 [engineer7 §R39.15 item 4a / §R39.17 §4, lead 2026-08-20] irc_*_rcfc = TS 잡의 **freq 단계**(수렴된 TS 의 Hessian, guess 기하의 CalcFC 아님)가 남긴 .chk 를 읽는 절감 route (11원자 80–260, 21원자 ~1,630 core-h/attempt). 🔴 스위치는 꺼져 있다(b0_reactions.json u56_2.irc_hessian_source=calcfc): dev box 에 G16 이 없어 rcfc 경로가 미검증이라 다음 제출의 route smoke 이후 lead 가 켠다. .chk 이관 배관(per-task 격리 포함)은 payload/U56.sh 에 이미 있다 — 켜면 그대로 동작해야 한다.
gaussian16._freq_smoke_legacy_note: [lead/user 2026-08-21, H2 3-deck smoke] `freq_smoke_legacy_generic` is SMOKE-ONLY: solvent.py raises SolventUndecided for it under purpose=production. It reproduces the abandoned generic+eps+EpsInf deck on H2 next to the acetone production deck so the two PCM parameter blocks, G(cav/disp/rep) terms and frequencies can be compared in one returned tree (decides whether the old generic certificate transfers, and the cost of the endpoint re-cert).
gaussian16._nosymm_p5_note: 🔴 [§39.89, proposer8, 2026-08-21] opt/opt_freq/freq/opt5 joined the list: all 22 P5 decks of the returned round lacked nosymm and Int(Grid=UltraFine) (the endpoint deck had both). One row (li_ec_radical_s0_L2) converged to an exactly planar structure (0.0000 Å heavy-atom deviation) -- the C-9/ADR-066 pathology that killed P1, now in P5. Applies to FUTURE decks only; the stored P5 geometries are NOT re-optimised (the freq-only recovery's n_imag is the audit that finds the symmetry-trapped rows). sp/force also carry Int(Grid=UltraFine) [proposer8 2026-08-21]: r_composite = (cheap opt+freq + high SP)/(cheap opt+freq) is a ratio between two METHODS if its halves use different grids, and the composite SP is a load-bearing energy. 🔴 Any r_composite/r_high measured before this change is NOT comparable to one measured after (none were -- P1b's freq halves died, §39.75).
gaussian16._nosymm_requirement: 🔴 B-2 (HANDOFF_CODER6 §B-2 / docs/05_STATE.md §0-k). Gaussian does not merely fail to break a degenerate starting guess -- it ACTIVELY RE-DETECTS the molecular point group and CONSTRAINS the optimisation to it. `guards.py`'s C-9 remedy (an explicit out-of-plane perturbation, `perturb_out_of_plane`) is INSUFFICIENT on its own for G16: perturbing an atom off a symmetry element accomplishes nothing if G16 re-detects the group within its own tolerance and re-imposes it on the very first optimisation step. Every job_type in `_nosymm_required_job_types` starts a TS search from a guess that may rely on that perturbation, or continues an IRC from a TS that does -- both must carry `nosymm` explicitly, not rely on the starting geometry alone. Cost: `nosymm` gives up the symmetry speedup, which is ZERO for a genuinely asymmetric species -- i.e. it costs nothing except on exactly the pathological (falsely-symmetric) cases this exists to guard against. 🔴 Do NOT read `nosymm`'s presence or absence off any ALREADY-STORED route string without first checking `route_echoed_is_complete` (criteria/g16.py, B-1) -- RT-1's three stored TS/IRC routes are truncated at 70 columns with no marker, and `nosymm`'s status on that run is [UNKNOWN], not absent. 🔴 ADR-099: `endpoint_opt_rough`/`endpoint_opt_freq` are in this list for the SAME reason as the TS routes above -- §0-g measured that a tight optimisation moves every interatomic distance and does NOT break an exact degeneracy, so a rough stage run without `nosymm` lets G16 re-impose the point group at step 1, and a certified-converged tight stage 2 would then certify the WRONG structure while every log says 'converged'.

_endpoint_two_stage._doc: 🔴 ADR-099 (user, direct ruling) / §39.32(h) (proposer6). Two-stage endpoint preparation for payload/P1.sh's reactant and product: STAGE 1 rough/loose optimisation (get into the basin cheaply), STAGE 2 tight opt+freq FROM stage 1's converged geometry (the certification). This does NOT relax C-8/C-8.1-8.3 -- the certification is still `endpoint_opt_freq` with n_imag == 0 at the level the TS search runs at; stage 1 is a cheaper approach to the same endpoint, not a substitute for it.
_endpoint_two_stage.perturbation: the C-9 out-of-plane perturbation (guards.perturb_out_of_plane) is applied ONCE, BEFORE stage 1, and is NOT re-applied between stage 1 and stage 2 -- re-kicking a geometry that stage 1 already converged would displace it off a real minimum, which is a worse error than the one being guarded against. If stage-1 exit is STILL on the symmetry element despite the kick and `nosymm` (i.e. `nosymm` was lost -- B-2), the correct response at stage 2 is its own CalcFC imaginary eigenvector, a MEASURED direction, strictly better than another random kick -- not implemented as an automatic restart here (see H-5/C-8 escalation in HANDOFF_CODER8.md), but the diagnosis (`stage1_exit_structural_set`'s point-group fingerprint) is emitted so a human/later automation can act on it. Both stages carry `nosymm` regardless (see _nosymm_required_job_types above) -- the perturbation and nosymm are two different, both-necessary defences against the same failure mode.
_endpoint_two_stage.job_structure: 2 PBS jobs per attempt (one per endpoint: reactant, product), submitted in PARALLEL. EACH job runs stage 1 then stage 2 internally, sequentially -- the stage1->stage2 handoff is a file read (stage 1's converged geometry becomes stage 2's input), not a separate resource request, so it is NOT a third job.
_endpoint_two_stage.budget_note: cumulative across BOTH internal stages, per endpoint -- same cap that already covers restarts elsewhere in this package. A wall-clock abort during either stage records which stage was running at kill (`stage1_budget_exhausted` / `stage2_budget_exhausted`, never collapsed into one token) and is NEVER recorded as `non_converged` -- a wall-clock abort is an EXECUTION fact, convergence is a CHEMICAL fact (C-2's principle, a fourth instance).
_endpoint_two_stage._rough_level_status: ✅ [RULED, Q2, proposer6/§39.38] rough runs at the SAME level (functional/basis/solvent/grid) as tight -- only the convergence thresholds move (opt=loose,maxcycles=100 vs opt=tight,calcfc,maxcycles=200). There is therefore no separate 'rough_level' key: the endpoint script passes the SAME level key to both `endpoint_opt_rough` and `endpoint_opt_freq`. Rationale (recorded here, not restated by whoever reads it later): (i) a cheaper rough surface can order near-degenerate coordination isomers differently, stage 1 SELECTS a basin on that surface, stage 2 then certifies honestly INSIDE it -- n_imag==0 is true and every internal check is consistent, so the wrong-minimum error is invisible; Li+ coordination isomers (U-55) sit closer together than any cheap surface's own error. (ii) stage 1 produces a GEOMETRY (no claim); stage 2 produces the CERTIFICATE -- same-level costs nothing extra because stage 1 was already going to be re-optimised at tight thresholds regardless. (iii) `nosymm` on BOTH stages (not same-level) is what actually prevents the wrong-surface failure now -- a symmetric stage 1 costs a restart at tight price, not correctness, PROVIDED `nosymm` survived stage 1. That is exactly why `nosymm` is required and checked on `endpoint_opt_rough` too, not only `endpoint_opt_freq` -- 'it's only a rough opt' is the sentence that most easily forgets it.
_endpoint_two_stage.f1_observables: src/pilot_package/config/f1_required_observables.json -- the binding emit-list. A merged pilot that reports only cost and convergence has NOT run F1.

_composite._doc: 🔴 ADR-032 composite 단가비 r_composite 측정 (engineer §R16.6 RT-1b).
_composite.r_composite: (cost(A) + cost(C)) / cost(A),  A=G-3 opt+freq,  C=G-1 SP on A 기하
_composite.gen_penalty: cost(G-4gen SP) / cost(G-4builtin SP) — **같은 기저**, gen 경로만 다르다
_composite.diffuse_penalty: cost(G-1 SP) / cost(G-4gen SP) — 둘 다 gen. diffuse 함수만 다르다
_composite._why_split: 🔴 engineer 는 '내장 def2TZVPP vs gen def2TZVPPD' 로 적었는데 그 비교는 gen 오버헤드와 diffuse 비용을 **섞는다**. 같은 기저를 두 경로로 넣어 gen 만 분리하고, diffuse 는 gen 안에서 따로 뺀다. 요청한 '분리'가 그렇게 해야 실제로 이뤄진다.
_composite.adr032_rule: |ΔG(composite − 전량고수준)| < 0.05 eV 채택 / 0.05~0.1 채택+σ_r 상향 / ≥ 0.1 불가
_composite._who_decides: 🔴 판정은 우리가 하지 않는다. 원자료(ΔG 3종)를 넘긴다.

_u27_noneq_smoke._doc: 🔴 [U-27] G16 에서 `NonEq` 가 **SMD 와 결합해** 도는가. 실측 확인 대상.
_u27_noneq_smoke.why: 되면 λ_out 전체가 G16 단일점만으로 끝난다(proposer §30.1). 안 되면 IEFPCM 로 λ_out 만 분리한다. 지금 안 물으면 왕복 1회(달력 3.5일)를 더 쓴다.
procedure: ① 중성 N 평형 SMD 최적화 (NonEq=write)
② 같은 기하 환원종 R, NonEq=read → G_R^vert
③ 같은 기하 환원종 R 평형 SMD → G_R^eq
_u27_noneq_smoke.what_we_measure: 🔴 λ_out 값이 아니라 **이 루트가 도는가**. 물리 판정은 proposer 몫.
_u27_noneq_smoke.fallback: SMD 가 거부되면 IEFPCM 로 같은 3단계를 재시도하고 어느 쪽이 통했는지 남긴다.
_u27_noneq_smoke.scope_guard: 대상 1종(P1b 가 쓰는 종 중 가장 작은 것). λ_out **본계산은 구현하지 않는다** — S1 파이프라인이고 착수 금지다.
_u27_noneq_smoke.chk_note: NonEq=read 는 ①이 남긴 .chk 를 읽는다 → 같은 디렉터리·같은 basename 이어야 한다.

_interpretation: 🔴 lead 지시는 'G-1 / G-2 두 레벨'이었고, 우리 payload 구조는 'level1(값싼) / level2(주)' 단가비 쌍이다. 매핑은 내가 정했다: level2 <- G-1(def2-TZVPPD, 주), level1 <- G-2(def2-TZVPD, 값싼/폴백). 근거는 TZVPD가 TZVPPD보다 작다는 것뿐이다. 이 매핑이 의도와 다르면 여기만 고치면 된다 — 셸에는 어디에도 박혀 있지 않다.
